items.claim: The row's forward seam carries the chapter's strongest Hebrew continuity signal at this point and goes undisclosed, while the one hazard the row does disclose is a WEB-side paragraph artifact with no Hebrew correlate.
items.evidence: Quotation hygiene is clean: the quoted run collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.10.14 and the English quotations are verbatim. The backward alternative the row rejects is byte-correct - the construct chain דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי (oshb:Eccl.10.12, byte) / דִּבְרֵי פִ֖יהוּ (oshb:Eccl.10.13, byte) is genuinely not reused at 10:14, whose noun is the absolute plural דְבָרִ֑ים (oshb:Eccl.10.14, byte), and the header-vs-genitive discipline holds since 10:12 is a genitive site and not a header. The defect is on the other seam. 10:14|10:15 is one of only 3 content-token-sharing adjacent verse pairs in MT ch 10 (sweep: 3 of 19 adjacent pairs), and the shared token is the negated-knowledge verb itself: לֹא יֵדַ֤ע (oshb:Eccl.10.14, byte) beside לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע (oshb:Eccl.10.15, byte). That is a byte-true construction straddling the row's own forward seam, and the row discloses nothing about it; its rejected_alternative litigates only the backward option, which is the one the bytes support least, since the catchword binding 10:12 to 10:13 does not extend to 10:14. The hazard the row does name - the WEB continuation-paragraph fold, correctly one of only 2 fold sites book-wide - is tier-4 English rendering metadata with no counterpart in the pointed text, so the row's confidence is calibrated on the witness where its seam evidence is weakest.

items.claim: The row's stated boundary ground - that the two verses share no construction - is byte-false: both carry a negated qal of the knowing root, and that pair is one of only three catchword-adjacent pairs in the chapter.
items.evidence: The quoted run collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.10.15 and the English quotations are verbatim, so the engagement class is met; the failure is in the warrant. Both verses carry the negative particle plus a qal of the same root: לֹא יֵדַ֤ע (oshb:Eccl.10.14, byte; prefix conjugation) and לֹֽא יָדַ֖ע (oshb:Eccl.10.15, byte; suffix conjugation). A contiguous consonantal sweep of that two-word sequence returns 6 verses book-wide (MT 4:13, 6:5, 8:5, 9:12, 10:14, 10:15), and 10:14/10:15 is the only adjacent-verse pair among them. At token level the same seam is 1 of only 3 content-token-sharing adjacent pairs in MT ch 10 (sweep: 3 of 19 adjacent pairs), and the shared token is precisely that root. The row's own device_notes concede a not-knowing motif shared with the preceding verse, which contradicts the rejected_alternative in the same row. The boundary may still stand on subject and topic grounds - the subjects differ and nothing else is shared - but the ground actually stated does not survive at byte tier and has to be re-cut.

items.claim: The cluster cohesion is byte-true and in fact understated, but the repeated element is mislabelled a construct phrase and the royal-vocabulary signal names a device object that excludes both of the row's own verses.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs collate at BYTE tier, and the repetition is byte-identical down to the cantillation: the longest common byte substring of the two verses spans אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ (oshb:Eccl.10.16) against אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ (oshb:Eccl.10.17), 25 codepoints. Three corrections. First, that is not a construct phrase: the first word carries zaqef qaton (U+0594), a disjunctive accent, in both verses, and what follows is the relative particle prefixed to a noun bearing a second-person feminine suffix, שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ - a suffixed noun cannot stand as nomen rectum, and the row's own gloss (land, whose king) and both witnesses' renderings treat the sequence as address plus relative clause, not as a genitive chain. Second, the cohesion is stronger than claimed: the pair shares four content tokens, the second repetition being וְשָׂרַ֖יִךְ בַּבֹּ֥קֶר יֹאכֵֽלוּ (oshb:Eccl.10.16, byte) against וְשָׂרַ֨יִךְ֙ בָּעֵ֣ת יֹאכֵ֔לוּ (oshb:Eccl.10.17, byte), which makes this the single strongest adjacency in MT ch 10 (sweep: only 3 of 19 adjacent pairs share any content token at all) - an under-cited strength, given that the sentence-zone default demands named byte cohesion before a cluster is allowed. Third, the royal-vocabulary device object cited for the chapter-end echo has 9 member verses (MT 1:1, 1:12, 2:12, 4:14, 5:8, 8:2, 8:4, 9:14, 10:20) and contains neither 10:16 nor 10:17: the royal word here is the suffix-bound שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ, which escapes a final-kaf sweep of the bare noun (final-letter allography), so the echo with מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל תְּקַלֵּ֔ל (oshb:Eccl.10.20, byte) must be argued from the suffixed form rather than from that object's membership.

items.claim: The one-verse unit at 10:18 is byte-supported: the quoted run is byte-true, the verse is a complete two-colon sentence in the Hebrew, and both of the row's seams carry zero shared content tokens.
items.evidence: בַּעֲצַלְתַּ֖יִם יִמַּ֣ךְ הַמְּקָרֶ֑ה collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.10.18, and the colon the row does not quote, וּבְשִׁפְל֥וּת יָדַ֖יִם יִדְלֹ֥ף הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Eccl.10.18, byte), completes the sentence inside the same verse - so the one-verse span is a whole sentence in the pointed text and not only in the English rendering, which is what the sentence-zone default requires. Cross-seam check: shared content tokens are 0 for 10:17|10:18 and 0 for 10:18|10:19, and MT ch 10 carries only 3 content-token-sharing adjacent pairs out of 19, neither of them at this row's seams - so the rejected_alternative's claim that the following verse reuses no lexeme here is byte-confirmed rather than merely thematic. Disclosure symmetry is owed nothing: the ch-10 ketiv/qere inventory is MT 10:3, 10:10 and 10:20 only, and no paseq seg and no parashah seg falls anywhere in ch 10 (the book carries 1 petuchah and 3 setumah segs, none in this chapter). One non-blocking observation: the two cola are semantically parallel rather than synthetic, but that label sits in device_notes as texture and drives no boundary.

items.claim: Byte-clean single sentence at 10:19, and the row's no-repeated-lexeme ground holds at byte tier against both the adjacent verses and the non-adjacent pair it names.
items.evidence: לִשְׂחוֹק֙ עֹשִׂ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.10.19, and the verse closes as one sentence with וְהַכֶּ֖סֶף יַעֲנֶ֥ה אֶת הַכֹּֽל (oshb:Eccl.10.19, byte), so the span is a complete Hebrew sentence. Shared content tokens with every candidate neighbour are zero: 10:19 against 10:18, against 10:20, and against each of 10:16 and 10:17. The resemblance the rejected_alternative had to dispose of is a semantic field and not a lexical link - the eating and drinking words of the royal pair are the shared verb of eating at 10:16 and יֹאכֵ֔לוּ (oshb:Eccl.10.17, byte) together with בַשְּׁתִֽי (oshb:Eccl.10.17, byte), and none of them shares a lexeme with לֶ֔חֶם or וְיַ֖יִן (oshb:Eccl.10.19, byte) here - so the ground is byte-true as stated. The row also correctly refrains from claiming an enjoyment site: the eat-and-drink co-occurrence object has 5 members (MT 2:24, 3:13, 5:17, 8:15, 9:7) and this verse is not one of them. No ketiv/qere note, paseq seg or parashah seg touches this verse.

items.claim: The opener claim and the imperative label both hold only in the English: in the Hebrew the quoted clause is not verse-initial and the negated form is not an imperative.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.10.20, and the ketiv/qere disclosure is correct - MT 10:20 is one of the 12 K/Q notes, and הכנפים כְּנָפַ֖יִם (oshb:Eccl.10.20, byte) is genuinely the inline unpointed ketiv followed by the pointed qere as the source bytes carry it, with no crosswalk qualifier owed since ch 10 lies outside the offset zone. Three defects. First, the verse does not open with the quoted clause: its first two words are גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ (oshb:Eccl.10.20, byte), and מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל תְּקַלֵּ֔ל (oshb:Eccl.10.20, byte) begins only at the third word - the claimed opening is the English word order, so the positional claim is translation-dependent and the Hebrew contests it. Second, אַל תְּקַלֵּ֔ל (oshb:Eccl.10.20, byte) is not an imperative: the taw preformative marks a prefix-conjugation second-person form, and Hebrew negates a command with that particle plus the prefix conjugation, never with the imperative; the contrast is visible inside this same cluster, where שַׁלַּ֥ח (oshb:Eccl.11.1, byte), תֶּן (oshb:Eccl.11.2, byte) and זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte) are true imperatives while אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte) is again the negated form. The doubling the row names is itself byte-true - the two-word negated sequence occurs twice in this verse. Third, the unit_type ground offered discriminates by verse count rather than by form, which is tier-4 metadata; at form level this verse carries the same negated-jussive counsel frame as the imperative zone that follows, and that is what the ruling has to be argued against.

items.claim: The imperative-pair warrant is byte-true, but the row's forward seam carries an undisclosed byte-true repeated phrase that is one of only two content-token-sharing adjacent pairs in the chapter.
items.evidence: The warrant class is satisfied: שַׁלַּ֥ח לַחְמְךָ֖ (oshb:Eccl.11.1, byte) and תֶּן חֵ֥לֶק (oshb:Eccl.11.2, byte) both collate at BYTE tier and both are genuine imperatives, which is the form the counsel-unit bounds are meant to be argued from, and the back seam is clean (0 shared content tokens across 10:20|11:1). The defect is the forward seam, which the row neither discloses nor answers: the two-word phrase repeats across it, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, byte) against עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, byte). A contiguous consonantal sweep of that phrase returns 7 verses book-wide (MT 5:1, 8:14, 8:16, 10:7, 11:2, 11:3, 12:7), and 11:2/11:3 is the only adjacent-verse pair among the seven. At token level the same seam is 1 of only 2 content-token-sharing adjacent pairs in all of MT ch 11 (sweep: 2 of 9 adjacent pairs). A word-for-word repeated phrase across adjacent verses is exactly the cohesion test this same cluster applies to bind 10:16 to 10:17; applied consistently it argues continuity across this seam, so the standing cross-seam rule requires it to be disclosed and rebutted rather than passed over.

items.claim: The span's stated cohesion warrant is absent from half its verses and has its first member inside the adjacent row, the required imperative/jussive frame is never derived, and the cited wind signal names device objects that are byte-absent from the whole chapter.
items.evidence: All three quoted runs collate at BYTE tier against the verses actually cited (the second sits at 11:5, as the row's own wording indicates, not at 11:6). Four defects. First, the negated-knowledge clause named as the binder occurs in ch 11 at exactly three verses - the two-word negated sequence at 11:2 and 11:5, and the negated-existential-plus-participle at 11:5 and 11:6 (sweeps: 2 verses each) - so it is absent from 11:3 and 11:4 and covers only 2 of the span's 4 verses. Second, the row itself records that the binder's first member is row-external at 11:2, which concedes that the device unites 11:2-11:6 and therefore cannot distinguish this span from one beginning a verse earlier; the disclosure is present but the rebuttal the cross-seam rule requires is not. Third, the counsel-unit bounds are supposed to be argued from the imperative/jussive frame and no such derivation is offered: the span's only imperative is זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte), paired with the negated jussive אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte), while 11:3 is a conditional indicative and 11:4 turns on a participle plus לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte); the zone's other two imperatives, שַׁלַּ֥ח (oshb:Eccl.11.1, byte) and תֶּן (oshb:Eccl.11.2, byte), sit outside the span, so the seam as drawn cuts the imperative frame in half and leaves three of four verses in an admonition unit carrying no directive form at all. Fourth, the wind signal names the chasing-wind and striving-of-spirit phrase objects, which are byte-absent from ch 11 entirely (7 verses: MT 1:14, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26, 4:4, 4:6, 6:9; and 2 verses: MT 1:17, 4:16) - a resh-ayin-family object error of exactly the catalogued class; the actual ch-11 tokens are the bare ר֖וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte) and הָר֔וּחַ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, byte), which belong to the any-ruach object (20 verses). Byte evidence that would have carried the span goes uncited: הֶעָבִ֥ים (oshb:Eccl.11.3, byte) against בֶעָבִ֖ים (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte), the cloud lexeme, 3 verses book-wide (MT 11:3, 11:4, 12:2), and the sowing root at לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, byte) against זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, byte), 2 verses book-wide - prefix-varied forms that escape token-equality adjacency and have to be swept per attested spelling.
